title: Start plugins in dependency order
description:
Each plugin lists the plugins it requires. Write

```cpp
std::vector<std::string> startOrder(const std::map<std::string, std::vector<std::string>>& requires_, std::vector<std::string>& problems);
```

`requires_` maps every **available** plugin to the names it requires. Return the order to start them in, and fill `problems` with one line per plugin that cannot start:

- Visit plugins in **alphabetical** order; for each, start its requirements first (in the order listed, depth first), then the plugin itself, each only once.
- A plugin whose requirement is **not available** cannot start: `"<plugin> needs <missing>"`. Any plugin that requires a plugin that cannot start also cannot start: `"<plugin> needs <requirement>"`.
- A plugin that is part of a **cycle** (it requires itself directly or through others) cannot start: `"<plugin> is part of a cycle"`. Plugins that require a plugin in a cycle cannot start either, with the `needs` message.
- Each plugin gets at most one problem line: the first reason found. Problems are listed in the order they are discovered.

```
requires_: { fog: [], seasons: [fog, weather], weather: [], storms: [weather, wind] }
order:     fog, weather, seasons
problems:  "storms needs wind"
```
hints: Give each plugin a state: not visited, being visited, started, failed. Reaching a plugin that is "being visited" means you have gone round a cycle.
Report each plugin's problem once. A helper `fail(plugin, line)` that does nothing if the plugin already failed keeps that simple.
